text:
### Observed differences

- The order between two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A26 came before A35, A36 and A41 in 98–100 in 100 traces, and A27 came before those same three activities in 98.5–100 in 100 (each pair occurs together in every trace in both windows). In the later window this is inverted: A35, A36 and A41 each come before A26 in 98–99.5 in 100 traces and before A27 in 98–98.5 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- Relative positions shifted accordingly: A35, A36 and A41 each moved from a mean relative position of about 0.58–0.59 of the trace to about 0.41 (earlier by roughly a sixth of the trace), while A27 moved from about 0.38 to 0.47 and A26 from about 0.53 to 0.62 (both later). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

- The transitions at the boundaries of the two groups changed. A25 led to A27 in 99 in 100 traces before; in the later window it leads to A35, A36 and A41 in roughly equal thirds (about 33 in 100 each) and to A27 in under 1 in 100. A26 led to A41, A35 and A36 (about 37, 34 and 28 in 100) before; in the later window it leads to A30 in 98.5 in 100. Each of A35, A36 and A41 led to A30 in about 28–37 in 100 before; in the later window each leads to A27 in about 32–34 in 100 and to A30 in under 1 in 100. The internal cycling among A35, A36 and A41 itself looks similar in both windows. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- Step distances match: the gap from A25 to A27 was 1 step in 99 in 100 traces before and is 4 steps in about 93 in 100 after; the gap from A26 to A30 was 4 steps in about 93 in 100 before and is 1 step in 98.5 in 100 after. Adjacencies that held in about 200 of 200 traces before (A26 into each of A35/A36/A41; each of A35/A36/A41 out to A30) now appear in only 1–2 traces, while A25→A35 and A35→A27 grew from 1 trace before to about 199 in 200 after (the before-side of these two rests on a single observation). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two blocks of activities exchanged their order. In the earlier window, traces typically ran A25, then A27 (mean position about 0.38), then A26 (about 0.53), then the group A35/A36/A41 (about 0.58), which cycled among its three members and exited to A30. In the later window, A25 leads directly into the A35/A36/A41 group (mean position about 0.41), the group exits to A27 (about 0.47), A26 follows (about 0.62) and closes with a direct transition to A30 — the group A35/A36/A41 now sits between A25 and the pair A27/A26 instead of after it. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG003]

The order reversal is shown directly by relational evidence for all six cross-pairs, with both activities of every pair co-occurring in all traces in both windows, so this is an ordering change rather than a participation change; the successor, position and gap shifts all point the same way, each difference exceeds what about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits produce, and screening flagged 26 items where about 0.41 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically yields. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003]

Limitations: the evidence shows relative order and positions within traces (event positions, not clock time), so it cannot distinguish one coordinated exchange of the two blocks from two separate shifts — the group moving earlier while A27/A26 move later — that leave the same traces; the indicators also overlap heavily, so the items are not independent confirmations, and a few gap items rest on only 1–2 observations. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
